prize_parts.citation: For the theoretical prediction of flat bands in twisted bilayer graphene at magic angles and the experimental discovery of correlated insulating and superconducting states in magic-angle graphene, opening the field of moire quantum matter

statement.case_for: After the full first-round exchange I keep magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene as my preferred single-part prize, and I want to say precisely why. What I look for is a mechanism simple enough to write on one page, whose consequence is a new experimental regime that was then actually realised. The Bistritzer-MacDonald continuum model is that: interlayer tunnelling renormalises the Dirac velocity to zero at discrete angles, and the 2018 experiments found correlated insulators and superconductivity in exactly that structure. The chain from prediction to decisive experiment runs through the three credited people, and the effect has since been reproduced by many independent groups and carried into twisted TMDs and other moire families, so the maturity test the colleagues who prefer clocks apply (independent reproduction) is met for the existence of the phases. The unsettled pairing mechanism is a follow-up question, and the citation I propose says nothing about it. I have moved on one point only: the argument that a clock prize should wait for the redefinition of the second did not survive Kroll, Johansson, Lindroth and Pearce. The redefinition is a consequence and not a condition of the discovery, so I no longer rest any part of my ranking on it. My remaining reservation about B057 is about discovery content versus refinement, not timing.
statement.case_against: B015 is about eight years old, the microscopic origin of the superconductivity is open, and the credit is exposed on three sides: Yuan Cao and the other experimental co-leads, the Dean group and related moire experiments, and earlier twisted-bilayer theory by Lopes dos Santos, Peres and Castro Neto. Four members treat the age as a real discount, and I cannot dismiss that. Against my own preference, B057 is the strongest case for attribution cleanliness (Katori and Ye in every proposal) and for breadth of support, with four members now putting it first. If the committee decides that the B015 credit history cannot be defended within three names, I would accept B057 with a citation built on the magic-wavelength lattice concept rather than B053, whose allocation problem (Mele or Hasan, with Bernevig, Hughes, Zhang and Fu outside) I find harder to resolve than the B015 one.

responses.point: Kroll argues that the redefinition of the second is a consequence and not a condition of the clock discovery, that waiting makes the credit picture harder, and that a model predicting a magic angle is a different kind of evidence from a measurement agreeing at the 1e-18 level.
responses.response: I concede the timing point: the Nobel criterion is the discovery, and the legal adoption of a new second should not drive our schedule. I have dropped it. I do not concede the second half. For B015 the relevant comparison is not a model against a measurement but a quantitative prediction (the magic-angle condition for flat bands) against an experiment that found correlated insulators and superconductivity at that structure, and that is a stronger test than elegance alone. Your worry about twist-angle disorder is fair, but sample variability has not prevented reproduction of the phases by many groups. Where we still differ is what counts as a discovery: I weigh a new regime of matter above a record accuracy for an already-recognised line of optical metrology, and I would want the clock citation to say what is new in principle, the magic-wavelength lattice.

responses.point: Lindroth argues that lattice clocks are a third thing next to the 2005 comb (the ruler) and the 2012 ion control (a different architecture), that the magic-wavelength trick is a physics idea, and that maturity after decades of independent checking matters more than fashion.
responses.response: That distinction is persuasive and it moves me part of the way. The magic-wavelength condition is a genuine physics idea, the cancellation of the differential light shift, and I now regard B057 as a distinct achievement and not as mere engineering; I was too quick to call it a refinement. I still rank it below B015 because the many-body clock physics came after the concept and the decisive records are shared among groups, which is the credit-boundary risk you yourself name. On maturity I would ask you to separate age from confirmation: eight years is short, but the correlated phases have been confirmed by many groups, so the discount you apply is for the pairing mechanism, which the citation will not claim. I accept B057 as my first alternative.

responses.point: Danielsson prefers B053 with Kane, Mele and Molenkamp as the cleaner 2D chain, ranks B015 fifth for timing, and asks whether the first magic-angle experiments suffice before the superconducting mechanism is understood.
responses.response: We agree on the central point that splitting Kane and Mele misstates the history, and I would defend Kane, Mele and Molenkamp over Kane, Molenkamp and Hasan if the committee went there. Where I still differ is how much the missing credit weighs. Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang proposed HgTe, and Hasan's 3D photoemission opened the branch from which most later materials work came; a three-name 2D citation leaves both outside, while the 2016 prize already honoured topology in matter. On your direct question: the first magic-angle experiments are enough for the discovery claim because the insulating and superconducting states were reproduced, so a citation limited to their existence is secure without a pairing theory. I take your point that this makes B053 a more mature but more awkward second choice, and not a clearly weaker one.

responses.point: Olsson argues that the prize requires an original verified observation, not a settled mechanism, and prefers Kane, Molenkamp and Hasan for B053 because the 3D ARPES work is a separate decisive experiment, while asking that the Kane-Mele versus Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang record be checked closely.
responses.response: I agree with the first part entirely and it is why our first choice coincides. On B053 we still part: replacing Mele with Hasan rewards a second experiment but separates Kane from his co-author on the founding quantum spin Hall papers, and I do not think the committee could defend that. Your own request to check the Kane-Mele and Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang record points the same way, because the record of the 2D theory is what a Molenkamp citation rests on. For B015 your point that the 2018 observation was the original experiment, not a later and more elegant one, is the answer I would give to the credit exposure around Yuan Cao and the Dean group. I would add one caution to our shared position: Cao is a lead author, so the committee should be able to explain why the experimental credit goes to the group leader alone.

responses.point: Johansson now ranks B057 first on its secure reproduction record and clean pair, says magic-angle graphene is where the committee will converge in a few years, and is comfortable with it as an alternative.
responses.response: Thank you for the candour about moving from circuit QED, and for taking B015 as a fallback. The difference between us is whether the committee should wait the few years you foresee. The pairing mechanism is the thing that may take longer than that, and the existence of the correlated phases does not depend on it, so I would not tie the timing to it. I do agree with you that the clock citation should rest on the magic-wavelength lattice concept and its realisation at 1e-18, and not on the future second, and if the committee goes to B057 I would support that wording. I also recognise your own caution about outside-field judgment, and I extend the same to myself on the atomic-physics side.

uncertainties: Whether the priority of the flat-band prediction over earlier twisted-bilayer theory can be settled so that the Bistritzer-MacDonald credit survives scrutiny.
Whether eight years and an open pairing mechanism clear the committee's maturity standard, given that four members treat age as a discount.
Whether Yuan Cao and the Dean group should enter the credit, and how that interacts with the three-person limit.
Whether the committee will weigh breadth of agreement and attribution cleanliness (B057) above field-opening novelty (B015), and whether I am overweighting simplicity of mechanism as a criterion.
Whether a B053 prize could name Mele or Hasan alongside Kane and Molenkamp without a defensible loss.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from the provided profile: I have no collaboration with any credited candidate on B015, B057 or B053. I note only that Johansson and Olsson are in the Gothenburg physics environment, which is an institutional proximity and not a scientific connection to any shortlisted discovery. I have no update to this disclosure after reading the other members' notes (Johansson's and Kroll's WACQT ties bear on B021, Kroll's JILA background on B057, neither on my preferred part).
